purpose: Apply the reusable network response-validity gate to the independent Dominguez-Garcia et al. 2026 annual plant-pollinator response before interpreting the external axis result as ecological-state replication.

source.article: Dominguez-Garcia et al. 2026 Ecology Letters e70293

published_sampling.rounds: twice monthly for at least seven rounds per year through the flowering season
published_sampling.transect: 100 m for 30 min per site per round
published_sampling.uneven_effort: number of rounds differs among years
published_effort_sensitivities: repeat analyses after removing annual singleton species
annual iNEXT sample coverage; most site-year combinations exceed 0.7

reason: The published sampling diagnostics are meaningful robustness checks, but the public processed response used for the external axis analysis is an annual binary recorded-link surface. It does not provide dyad-level repeated-detection histories or independent true-absence information sufficient to identify latent link gain/loss.
consequence_for_external_axis_result: The pre-frozen gain/loss axis comparison remains a valid out-of-site predictive pattern for recorded annual links. It is not a detection-defensible cross-system replication of latent ecological assembly/disassembly mechanisms.
not_a_claim_about_source_paper: This response-validity classification does not invalidate the source paper's own structural-persistence analyses or its published effort sensitivities. It limits this project's reuse of the annual binary link surface for mechanistic gain/loss replication.
claim_ceiling: Describe the independent result as cross-site replication or non-replication of observed-link predictive information only. Do not use it as evidence that plant-side or pollinator-side opportunity universally controls latent ecological gain/loss, and do not use it as routeability evidence.
binary_detection_material_interpretation: The source paper reports high/consistent network-level coverage and singleton sensitivity, so material bias is not asserted here; however absence of evidence for material bias is not treated as validation of dyad-level latent absence.
